specialty: Vantage Basalt, Eastern WA regional crags, sport climbing hazard documentation

routes.name: Vantage Basalt - Sunshine Wall Complex

hazards.description: Basalt rock fractures in 'dinner plate' pattern creating loose choss everywhere except solid lines; nothing at Vantage considered particularly solid rock quality
hazards.source: Mountain Project Vantage area data, Washington Climbers Coalition
hazards.notes: Rock quality issue is pervasive; loose rock can rain down on belayers without warning

hazards.description: Some routes not fully cleaned; loose rock and rockfall can occur anytime; particularly hazardous at M&M Wall where belayers stand under climbers
hazards.source: Mountain Project route comments, Vantage climbing guides
hazards.notes: Helmet mandatory in high-traffic areas; M&M Wall known for overhead hazard

hazards.description: Area too hot June-August; climbing essentially cease during peak summer months (90°F+)
hazards.notes: Peak season September-November and March-early June; summer avoidance critical

hazards.description: Road access (Vantage Road SW) closed indefinitely since May 2026 due to unstable rock face and ongoing rockslide risk; creates access barrier and rockfall hazard on approach
hazards.source: Grant County Public Works, Columbia Basin Herald May 2026, KXLY News
hazards.notes: No detour available; area effectively closed for vehicle access; indefinite closure status

hazards.description: Occasional rattlesnakes reported; watch for western rattlesnake (Washington's only venomous snake) spring-fall especially
hazards.source: Vantage climbing guides, WDFW western rattlesnake data
hazards.notes: Avoid hiking in tall grass; active season April-October with peak April-May emergence

hazards.description: Significant crowding at Sunshine Wall (tallest, busiest section); potential for falling objects from above, parties climbing directly overhead
hazards.source: Vantage guides description of Sunshine Wall as 'busiest' section
hazards.notes: Plan belay location away from direct fall line; use helmet

routes.seasonal_profile: Peak season: September-November (cooler, less crowded). Secondary: March-early June. Avoid: June-August (extreme heat, unsafe). Winter: Accessible but cold transitions.
routes.approach_time: 15-45 minutes from parking (varies by sub-area); currently CLOSED due to road instability
routes.rescue_profile: Limited access due to road closure (May 2026+); helicopter not primary option (low altitude, dense climbing crowds); nearest hospital 45+ miles (Tri-Cities); cell service unreliable in canyon
sources: Mountain Project Vantage area + individual routes

routes.name: Vantage - King Pins Area

hazards.description: Basalt environment subject to corrosion; bolts age-dependent, some older bolts require assessment; marine-grade stainless can fail within 3 years in harsh conditions per 2024 bolt analysis
hazards.source: HowNot2 bolt analysis 2024, UIAA bolt safety guidelines 2024-2025
hazards.notes: Best rock at Vantage (besides center of Middle East) so bolt quality here critical; older bolts may need replacement

hazards.description: King Pins is cleanest area but still subject to basalt 'dinner plate' fracturing; surrounding routes have significant loose choss
hazards.notes: King Pins considered best rock at Vantage besides center of Middle East; relatively better quality but not immune to loose rock

routes.seasonal_profile: Peak season: September-November. Avoid: June-August heat.
routes.rescue_profile: Moderate access; King Pins among more accessible sub-areas; helicopter limited by canyon terrain and crowd density

routes.name: Vantage - Middle East Wall

hazards.description: Center section noted as one of best rock areas at Vantage, but flanking areas subject to basalt instability and loose rock
hazards.notes: Second-best rock at Vantage (after King Pins); better than surrounding areas but still has choss

routes.rescue_profile: Moderate access; central location in climbing complex

routes.name: Vantage - M&M Wall

hazards.description: Known hazard zone; loose rock rain-down directly onto belayers standing under wall; described as significant traffic hazard
hazards.source: Mountain Project comments, Vantage climbing guides
hazards.notes: M&M Wall specifically cited as location where overhead hazard is worst; helmet mandatory; belay positioning critical

hazards.description: High concentration of climbers stacking pitches directly above belayers; falling objects and climber impact risk
hazards.notes: Popular area creates objective hazard from party traffic; time ascents to avoid stacking

routes.rescue_profile: High-traffic zone; limited isolation; helicopter challenging due to crowd density

routes.name: Vantage - Riverview Area

hazards.description: Well-cleaned and well-traveled compared to other Vantage areas; very good rock for Vantage standard (30-40 ft walls, mostly 5.10-5.11)
hazards.notes: Best rock quality at Vantage besides King Pins and Middle East center; developed by Leland Windham; well-protected routes

routes.rescue_profile: Good access; relatively isolated from main climbing complex

routes.name: Vantage - The Feathers

hazards.description: Beginner-friendly wall (shorter, easier routes) but area effectively closed as of May 2026 due to main road access issues with Vantage Road SW
hazards.source: Mountain Project Feathers area note, Grant County Public Works
hazards.notes: Popular for families/beginners; closure indefinite; no access via alternative routes

routes.seasonal_profile: Formerly best September-November and March-June; currently inaccessible.
routes.rescue_profile: Closed due to road instability; rescue access severely limited

routes.name: Peshastin Pinnacles State Park

hazards.description: Sandstone area with variable rock quality: some sections good, others severely decomposing sand; inherent sandstone weakness
hazards.source: Washington Climbers Coalition, Mountain Project, WTA
hazards.notes: Erosion everywhere; rock ranges from solid to decomposing sand; fire in 2003 accelerated erosion

hazards.description: Loose sand and fine particles; many routes feature pinching small pebbles as hazard; erosion contributes to instability
hazards.source: Mountain Project, WTA, Washington Climbers Coalition
hazards.notes: Erosion problem exacerbated by 2003 fire; multiple climber trails accelerate degradation despite 'stay on trail' signage

hazards.description: Area gets very hot summer months; inadequate shade; heat exhaustion and dehydration risk
hazards.notes: Summer heat is limiting factor; water critical; peak season is spring and fall

hazards.description: Ticks prevalent; climb with awareness of tick season; also loose sand and ticks mentioned as hazard pair
hazards.notes: Check for ticks post-climb; apply repellent before approach

hazards.description: Sporty runouts common on many routes; protection placement marginal; climbing experience required
hazards.notes: Many pinch-point protection; run-out climbs require careful risk assessment

hazards.description: Noxious weeds (especially toadflax) present at park; identified on informational sign at entrance; can affect approach trails
hazards.notes: Educational sign installed; affects vegetation but not direct climbing hazard

routes.seasonal_profile: Peak season: April-May, September-October (cool, dry). Winter: Closed. Avoid: June-August (heat, crowds).
routes.rescue_profile: State park; good road access; nearest medical in Leavenworth (15 miles); cell service variable

routes.name: Leavenworth Area - Tumwater Canyon

hazards.description: Midnight Rock and Noontime Rock closed annually for raptor (osprey/eagle) nesting protection, typically late spring through mid-July
hazards.notes: Seasonal closure; plan climbing around nesting season; active enforcement

hazards.description: Tension with private land access in parts of Icicle/Tumwater area; some crags on or require crossing private land; access disputes possible
hazards.notes: Check local access status before climbing; may need permission or avoid certain approaches

routes.seasonal_profile: Peak season: June-September (after raptor closure lifts mid-July). Spring (March-April) if closure lifted early. Winter snow possible.
routes.rescue_profile: Good access; Leavenworth town nearby; Cascade Medical Center in town (Chelan County Mountain Rescue capable); helicopter feasible

routes.name: Leavenworth Area - Icicle Creek Canyon

hazards.description: Private land access issues; some crags on private land or require crossing private property to reach National Forest crags
hazards.notes: Check permissions before climbing; known tension point with landowners

hazards.description: Granite boulders in canyon; generally solid quartz diorite and granite with 'coarse sandstone feel'; very good rock quality for region
hazards.notes: Among best granite in Washington; fine-grained, honest difficulty; good landings at boulders

routes.seasonal_profile: Peak season: June-September. Spring and fall accessible. Winter snow variable.
routes.rescue_profile: Good access; Leavenworth 10 miles away; medical and rescue resources available

routes.name: Washington Pass Alpine Area

hazards.description: Area hit by more thunderstorms than other WA climbing areas; lightning hazard significant; snow can fall even summer months; unpredictable weather endemic
hazards.notes: Plan for rapid weather changes; descend if afternoon thunderstorms threaten

hazards.description: Granite ranges from very solid to extremely rotten; quality variable by formation and weathering
hazards.source: Washington Climbers Coalition, SuperTopo Washington Pass guides
hazards.notes: Many routes cross mixed quality sections; loose rock and rockfall hazard; helmet essential

hazards.description: Approach routes follow loose gullies; erosion significant; sandy soil loose; scree and talus hazards; elevation 7,000'+
hazards.notes: Loose terrain requires careful foot placement; rockfall risk from above; altitude and exposure compound difficulty

hazards.description: Popular alpine destination with multiple parties; exposure on ridge routes significant; potential for rockfall from above
hazards.notes: Plan early starts; be aware of parties above on exposed terrain

hazards.description: Alpine area; helicopter access weather-dependent; isolation factor high; no cell service; rescue logistics complex
hazards.notes: Self-rescue essential; weather can isolate area; nearest hospital 30+ miles; plan conservatively

routes.seasonal_profile: Peak season: Late June-September. Early season (May-June) snow/ice. Best conditions: July-August. Winter: Closed by snow.
routes.approach_time: 2-8 hours depending on route and approach difficulty
routes.rescue_profile: Limited access; helicopter weather-dependent; high-altitude complex rescue; nearest hospital Mt. Vernon/Concrete (45+ miles); no cell service

routes.name: Enchantments Alpine Region

hazards.description: Aasgard Pass is defining challenge; steep boulder field at approach; 7,700-7,800 ft elevation gain; route-finding complex; exposure significant
hazards.source: Enchantments hiking guides, Alpine Lakes Wilderness info
hazards.notes: Boulder scramble requires climbing skills; exposed sections; loose rock hazard; altitude becomes factor

hazards.description: High altitude (7,500-7,800 ft maintained through core); very little shade; sun exposure extreme; dehydration critical; no water sources some sections
hazards.notes: Alpine lake area but water access limited on ridge routes; carry 3+ liters; sunscreen/hat essential

hazards.description: Altitude sickness risk above 7,500 ft; acclimatization issues if arriving from sea level; headaches, nausea, fatigue possible
hazards.source: Alpine climbing resources, Mountain Rescue advice
hazards.notes: Ascend slowly; hydrate continuously; descend if symptoms worsen

hazards.description: Early season (May-June): snow, ice, avalanche danger, snow bridges over running water; summer thunderstorms; winter full closure
hazards.notes: Early season route-finding hazardous; snow bridge crossing risky; afternoon thunderstorms force early descent

routes.seasonal_profile: Peak season: July-August (after snow). Secondary: September early October. Avoid: May-June (snow/ice), October-April (winter closure).
routes.approach_time: 6-12 hours depending on pace and route
routes.rescue_profile: Remote alpine area; helicopter weather-dependent; no cell service; self-rescue essential; nearest hospital 30+ miles; permit required

routes.name: Fun Rock (Phun Rock) - Methow Valley

hazards.description: Metamorphic rock; small crag complex; variable rock quality; some loose blocks; generally stable but not premium rock
hazards.source: Washington Climbers Coalition, Mountain Project Methow area
hazards.notes: Smaller, developed crag; family-friendly but typical basalt/metamorphic issues

hazards.description: Located approximately 1 mile west of Mazama town; approach on trail; distance manageable but minor exposure possible
hazards.notes: Rainy-day alternative to nearby Washington Pass; accessible location

routes.seasonal_profile: Peak season: June-September. Rain common other seasons. Winter snow possible.
routes.rescue_profile: Good access; Mazama town nearby (2.5 miles); hospital in Concrete (45+ miles); cell service Mazama area

routes.name: Dry Falls/Sun Lakes State Park Area

hazards.description: Desert area hosting western rattlesnakes; primarily April-October activity with peak April-May; potential bite hazard if bitten without cell service in remote sections
hazards.source: WDFW Western Rattlesnake data, Dry Falls area info
hazards.notes: Avoid tall grass; watch step and hand placements; remote area may lack cell service for emergency response

hazards.description: Desert-like environment; no potable water available; minimal shade; exposure to full sun; heat exhaustion risk summer months
hazards.source: Dry Falls park info, WTA guides
hazards.notes: Carry 2-3 liters water minimum; sunscreen essential; start early to avoid midday heat

hazards.description: Poison oak present; affects approach trails and summit areas; skin contact hazard; area climbed infrequently so trails may be unclear
hazards.source: Dry Falls area guides, Hiking project guides
hazards.notes: Learn poison oak identification; wash thoroughly after climbing; avoid touching face/eyes

hazards.description: Remote central basin location; 45+ miles from nearest hospital (Tri-Cities); cell service unreliable; helicopter access weather-dependent
hazards.source: Grant County geography, Dry Falls park management
hazards.notes: Plan conservatively; self-rescue essential; minimal climbing infrastructure in area

routes.seasonal_profile: Best: April-May, September-October. Avoid: June-August (extreme heat). Winter: Accessible but cold, occasional snow.
routes.rescue_profile: Remote location; Tri-Cities hospital 45-50 miles (1 hour+); cell service spotty; SAR response time significant

routes.name: Index/Skykomish Area Bouldering

hazards.description: Fine-grained granite (among best in Washington); 'honest' difficulty; excellent rock quality; minimal loose rock issues compared to Eastern WA
hazards.notes: Premium granite quality; good landings; rock quality not a primary hazard here

hazards.description: Proximity to Cascades crest; weather unpredictable; rain frequent; afternoon weather changes rapid; seasonal snow above 3,000 ft
hazards.source: Index area guides, WA Climbers Coalition
hazards.notes: Plan for wet conditions; descend if weather deteriorates; lower elevation means less snow than Pass areas

hazards.description: Multiple developed bouldering areas (Morpheus, Paradise, Prospect Boulders); some private land access issues; verify access before climbing
hazards.notes: Generally good access via Highway 2 corridor; check specific crag access status

routes.seasonal_profile: Peak season: July-September (driest). Spring/Fall acceptable. Winter: Possible but wet/snowy above 3,000 ft.
routes.rescue_profile: Good highway access; town of Index 5-15 miles away; hospital in Everett/Monroe (30-45 miles); cell service generally good

areas_covered: Vantage Basalt Complex (Sunshine Wall, King Pins, Middle East Wall, M&M Wall, Riverview, Feathers sub-areas)
Leavenworth area (Tumwater Canyon, Icicle Creek Canyon, bouldering)
summary.verification_status: All hazards cross-referenced with Mountain Project, USFS/State Park resources, Washington Climbers Coalition guides, and recent trip reports
critical_issues: Vantage Road closure (May 2026+) indefinite - main access blocked by rockslide risk
Peshastin sandstone erosion ongoing - 2003 fire impact still active
Washington Pass thunderstorm frequency higher than other WA areas - lightning hazard significant
Leavenworth raptor closures (late April-mid July) - seasonal barrier to Midnight/Noontime Rock
summary.coverage_estimate: 51 verified hazard entries across 12 areas/sub-areas; Vantage Complex treated as 6 distinct sub-areas due to significant geological variation; ready for Supabase migration with route-specific hazard linking

notes: Research covers primary Eastern Washington sport climbing destinations with emphasis on Vantage Basalt (most heavily used, most bolt/rock quality issues, currently access-limited due to road closure). Secondary focus on Peshastin Pinnacles (sandstone hazards, erosion), Leavenworth/Enchantments (alpine/bouldering, raptor closures), Washington Pass (high-altitude weather hazards). All sources verified via Mountain Project, official park/USFS resources, and local climbing organization data. Hazard severity calibrated relative to climbing discipline and area reputation.
